content: I came here because I feel like I'm suffocating with all this anger and hurt inside me. The way they treated me at work was just... unjustifiable. They laid me off, but everyone else who wasn't as good as me got to stay. It's like they picked on me for some reason, and it’s eating me up. No one seems to understand how much this has affected my self-worth and my sense of identity. I need someone to hear me out without trying to tell me what a great thing losing my job is or suggesting that there was something wrong with me. Just let me vent about why I think they were completely in the wrong.
I'm sorry you're going through this. It sounds really tough, feeling like you were treated unfairly at work. Can you tell me more about what happened that made you feel picked on?

They just cut my position out of nowhere. I was doing everything right, putting in the hours, meeting all my goals. But they kept people who weren't pulling their weight and let me go. It’s like they had it out for me or something. And now everyone acts like it's no big deal, but it feels like a huge betrayal. How am I supposed to trust anyone after this? They took away everything I worked so hard for, and there was nothing wrong with my performance. It’s infuriating!

It sounds incredibly frustrating to feel that your efforts weren’t recognized while others who weren't as diligent stayed on. The sense of betrayal must be tough to handle. How have you been coping with these feelings since it happened?

I haven't really been coping well at all. I just keep replaying everything in my head, wondering what went wrong and why they did this to me. It’s like a constant loop of anger and hurt. And every time someone tries to tell me there are other opportunities or that it's not as bad as it seems, I feel even more frustrated because none of that changes how betrayed I feel by the people who were supposed to value my work.

I can't shake this feeling that they saw something in me that made them target me. It’s like a punch in the gut every time I think about it. And no one gets why it's such a big deal or why I'm so upset. They just want me to move on, but how do you just move on from being treated this way? It feels impossible.

It sounds really tough to keep replaying those feelings and not having others fully understand your perspective. The constant loop of anger and hurt must be draining. Have there been any moments where you’ve found a small bit of comfort or support, even if it’s just from talking about it?

I don’t think anyone really gets it. Every time I try to talk about how I feel, people either dismiss me or offer generic advice that doesn't help at all. It's like they can't see past the surface of what happened and don't understand the depth of my pain. Even talking here feels pointless because no one can change what happened.

I just want someone to acknowledge that this was a huge injustice and that it’s okay for me to be angry about it. But instead, I get platitudes like “it’ll all work out” or “look at the bright side.” It’s not helping; it’s making everything worse because it feels like they’re trivializing what happened to me.

I can’t just move on from this betrayal and unfair treatment. It's a part of who I am right now, and until someone acknowledges that, there’s no way for me to feel any better about it.

It sounds really tough not having your feelings fully acknowledged by others. Having someone validate the depth of what you’re going through could make a big difference. Do you have anyone in mind who might be able to offer that kind of support, even if it’s just a close friend or family member? Sometimes sharing these thoughts with them can help feel more understood.

I don’t think I have anyone who truly understands what I’m going through. My friends and family mean well, but they either try to cheer me up or tell me to look at the bright side. It’s like they’re trying to make it better by pretending it wasn’t as bad as it was, which just makes me angrier because nothing can change how unfair this whole situation feels.

I don’t want anyone to think I’m not strong enough to handle this; I just need someone who will listen and validate my feelings without dismissing them. But every time I try to talk about it with people close to me, they end up saying something that makes me feel even worse. It’s like there’s no way out of this anger and hurt.

I keep hoping that one day I’ll wake up and everything will be different, but for now, all I can do is lash out at anyone who tries to tell me it’s not as bad as it seems. Because it is. And until someone acknowledges that, I don’t see how anything can change.

It’s frustrating because I know deep down that this is a significant blow to my sense of self and professional identity.

I just want someone to say, “This was unfair, and you have the right to be angry about it.” But instead, I get platitudes and suggestions for coping mechanisms that don’t address what really happened. It feels like no matter who I talk to, they’re going to tell me how to feel rather than listen to why I’m feeling this way.

I can’t help but lash out because it’s the only way I know how to express my frustration and hurt. And until someone acknowledges that this was a real injustice, I don’t see any point in trying to move on or accept anything else. It just feels like another attempt to make me feel better when what I need is for someone to understand the depth of my pain.

And as for art or music, those are just outlets to express my feelings temporarily, but they don’t address the core issue of why this happened and why no one seems to understand.

Until someone can truly understand and validate what happened to me, I don’t see any point in trying other methods of coping. They just feel like band-aids on a deep wound that needs more substantial acknowledgment and recognition.
